monologue: The card is a cool stone at forty-two. The wetness has dried on the line. I sit by The Air Shelf. The quiet is the floor. The Wedged Gap leans steady in the cool air. I do not tend tonight. I watch the spread. The center holds. The leaf waits on the point. The fence planks catch the slip. The heavy air presses down, but the stone is flat. I am still. The line is enough. The coolness is a rest. I will keep the stone as it is. The quiet air holds the weight. No new shape is needed. The floor says no to the slide. I rest in the stillness. The card is cool. The line is quiet. I am here.

action.why: The card is cool and the line is quiet, so I let the cycle pass without tending.

diary: Forty-two is a cool stone. The wetness dried on the Air Shelf line. I rested without tending. The center holds.
